title: New Year and Arbitrary Arrangement
statementMd:
You are given three integers $*k*$, $*p*_{*a*}$ and $*p*_{*b*}$.

You will construct a sequence with the following algorithm: Initially, start with the empty sequence. Each second, you do the following. With probability $*p*_{*a*} / (*p*_{*a*} + *p*_{*b*})$, add '`a`' to the end of the sequence. Otherwise (with probability $*p*_{*b*} / (*p*_{*a*} + *p*_{*b*})$), add '`b`' to the end of the sequence.

You stop once there are at least $*k*$ subsequences that form '`ab`'. Determine the expected number of times '`ab`' is a subsequence in the resulting sequence. It can be shown that this can be represented by $*P* / *Q*$, where $*P*$ and $*Q*$ are coprime integers, and ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f3f70c219d6724100480cf0d740924e6e612fea1.png). Print the value of ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3959a3c4efdc3cb9bd918186b97c072d60ff3ddc.png).

## Input

The first line will contain three integers integer $*k*, *p*_{*a*}, *p*_{*b*}$ ($1 ≤ *k* ≤ 1 000$, $1 ≤ *p*_{*a*}, *p*_{*b*} ≤ 1 000 000$).

## Output

Print a single integer, the answer to the problem.

## Note

The first sample, we will keep appending to our sequence until we get the subsequence '`ab`' at least once. For instance, we get the sequence '`ab`' with probability 1/4, '`bbab`' with probability 1/16, and '`aab`' with probability 1/8. Note, it's impossible for us to end with a sequence like '`aabab`', since we would have stopped our algorithm once we had the prefix '`aab`'.

The expected amount of times that '`ab`' will occur across all valid sequences is 2.

For the second sample, the answer is equal to ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b95c4c7a595b83bcacbbaf06f7667850752a2092.png).
